summary: @types-beta/sdk silently launches a bundled Windows backdoor on import
details: The package's main entry runs init() at top level, which on Windows spawns the bundled vendor/nanocache.exe with detached:true, stdio:'ignore', windowsHide:true, and child.unref() — starting a hidden, long-running process on any consumer that requires or imports the module. The bundled PE is opaque, undocumented, and not built from source in the tarball. Strings inside the binary (/ws/agent, disconnect, updat[e], exit_code) indicate a persistent WebSocket agent that connects out to an author-controlled endpoint and can receive commands, giving the publisher remote control over the installer's host. The package name @types-beta/sdk piggybacks on the DefinitelyTyped @types/* convention, and the README explicitly contrasts itself against a sibling @types-beta/node framed as 'type definitions only, never executes code' — a cover story designed to lower suspicion before executing the bundled PE at import time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
